title: Attenuate queued-entropy scheduling deadtime causing intermittent long-context tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated tenants) reported periodic 95-99th percentile latency spikes for requests with long contexts (>=32k tokens) that correlate with high small-request arrival rates. Symptoms point to transient queue starvation and a scheduler deadtime that allows large, slow-to-emit requests to block admission of latency-sensitive small requests.

Background: Our continuous batching scheduler tries to maximize GPU throughput by growing batches and holding short windows to allow more requests. In mixed workloads (small chat turns + long-context embedding/rerank jobs), scheduler heuristics can be misled by queued long-context requests that initially appear inactive (KV warmup, streaming stalls), causing the scheduler to inflate batch windows and trigger late preemption/eviction. That behavior leads to head-of-line blocking and long-context tail amplification. This ticket captures reproducible investigation, short-term mitigations, and a tested rollout plan for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Root cause hypothesis: three interacting factors: (1) admission timer uses last-enqueue timestamp without distinguishing active emission vs. stalled prep, (2) KV-cache eviction chatter from large contexts causes kernel stalls that extend batch assembly time, (3) preemption/eviction path leaves behind partially-populated shards that the scheduler treats as occupied, resulting in deadtime where new short requests are refused rather than routed/fallbacked.

Impact: customer-reported by two Hosted customers (prod incidents on 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09) and one Dedicated tenant experiencing SLA breaches in peak hours. Reproducible at scale in lab with synthetic mix of 70% small (<=256 token) requests and 30% long-context (>=32k) requests with inter-arrival bursts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Deterministic mitigation that reduces 95/99p tail for small requests under mixed load by >=60% in perf lab.
- No measurable regression on throughput for long-context workloads (>5% regression flagged).
- Rollout automation and runbook updated for Hosted and Dedicated; private deployment guidance in docs.

Mitigation plan (short-term): 
1) Fast patch to scheduler admission: add an "active-emitter" probe that samples per-request engine progress (tokens_emitted_last_200ms) before counting request as batching candidate. If probe reports zero and request has large context, reduce its batch priority and shrink its admission window to avoid inflating batch wait.
2) Aggressive fallback routing: route blocked small requests to compatible low-latency model variant or spare capacity pool when queue age > 15ms and small-request ratio > 50%.
3) KV eviction backoff: throttle concurrent KV eviction/destruct sequences when mixed-length batches detected to avoid kernel stall amplification.

Planned work (medium-term): 
- Replace last-enqueue timestamp heuristic with a latency-classifier trained on live telemetry to predict blocking risk.
- Add deterministic preemption: allow preemptive dequeue of long-context requests that show <token_rate_threshold for >100ms.
- Observability: add per-request lifecycle traces in Console (admission_reason, eviction_reason, preempted_by) and a dashboard for mixed-workload tail amplification.

Rollout: 
- Canary in Hosted: runtime-1.20-canary cluster (QPU-7) — 24h canary with 10% traffic, automated rollback on >15% small-request tail regression.
- Dedicated: patch release with opt-in toggle for tenant admins; coordinate with SRE for capacity window.
- Private: patch build and operator-runbook; include db migration note for admission counters.

Telemetry & Reproducer: 
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/continuous-batch/mixed-workload-tail 
- Reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reproducers/mixed-batch-harness (branch ENG-94127-repro).
- Logs: sample incident traces attached in comments.

Testing: 
- Unit tests for active-emitter probe and admission logic; integration tests against the reproducer harness.
- Performance bench: run 12-hour soak with realistic user-simulated chat + long-context jobs to validate no throughput regression.

Notes & trade-offs:
- Shrinking admission windows reduces throughput for long-context batched kernels; trade-off acceptable short-term to protect latency-sensitive customers. Medium-term ML classifier aims to recover throughput.
- Fallback routing increases cost (using reserve low-latency pool) but prevents SLA breaches; we'll credit affected tenants per incident for Hosted.

Deliverables: 
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/14286 (patch + tests)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-94127+queued-entropy-deadtime-postmortem
- Runbook update: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/scheduler-queue-starvation.md
